chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir, from ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Yazīd ibn Ḍamrah al-Laythī, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a man who will be occupied at the time of zawāl: may he perform it early from the beginning of the day? He said: “Yes. If he knows that he will be occupied, then he may bring it forward in the early part of the whole day.”

key_terms.أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ: Imam Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, the authority being asked for the ruling
key_terms.صَدْرِ ٱلنَّهَارِ: the early part of the day
key_terms.يَتَعَجَّلُ: to do something earlier or in advance
key_terms.يَشْتَغِلُ: to be occupied or preoccupied in a way that affects performing the act at its normal time
key_terms.ٱلزَّوَالِ: the time of the sun’s decline from the zenith, a recognized prayer time marker

ai.seo_question: Can a person perform a prayer earlier in the day if he expects to be busy at the time of zawāl?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning advancing a prayer due to expected occupation at the time of zawāl. Imam Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام permits performing it earlier in the day when one knows in advance that he will be unable to attend to it at its usual time.
